claims.text: Half-fill a 50 mL glass beaker with water. Seal one end of a capillary tube by heating it in a flame. Put a few drops of the organic liquid in an ignition tube and dip the open capillary end into it. Tie the ignition tube to the thermometer with its lower end near the thermometer bulb. Set the beaker on wire gauze on a tripod and position the thermometer bulb and half of the ignition tube in the water.
claims.rationale: Grouped paraphrase of manual procedure steps 1-5; no timing inferred.

quotes.exact_quote: 1. Take a 50 mL glass beaker and fill it half with water. 2. Take a capillary tube and seal its one end by heating it in the flame. 3. Transfer a few drops of the organic liquid compound in the ignition tube. Dip the open end of capillary tube into the liquid taken in the ignition tube.

4. Tie the ignition tube with the thermometer with the help of a thread in such a way that the lower end of the ignition tube is near the bulb of the thermometer. 5. Keep the 50 mL beaker on a wire gauze kept on a tripod stand. Fix the thermometer and the ignition tube with the help of thread in such a way that the bulb of the thermometer and half of the ignition tube are dipped in water.

claims.text: The thermometer bulb and half of the ignition tube are immersed in the bath; the bulb and ignition tube do not touch the beaker.
claims.rationale: Required setup state, not an experimentally measured outcome.
